content:
- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days); cap forecast growth after 2–3 consecutive days of high sentiment.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion within 5–7 days after a spike, model often fails to correct; apply downward bias in next 3–5 days if sentiment is fading.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate late-period prices (last 7–10 days) when sentiment is positive; add 1–2% buffer to end of forecast if sentiment > 0.67.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.67, -0.67, +0.67), model often misjudges direction; favor midpoint of sentiment range for next forecast.
